rows.title: The high-risk plants set's rulings records carry the decisions now in force
rows.detail: The plants set keeps its rulings in one ledger, and every entry of its conflicts register and every behaviour of its journey specification points at that ledger rather than holding an answer of its own. Decisions taken since the set's own sittings change plants behaviours that earlier ledger entries settled, and not one of them is in the ledger, so the set's own record reads the opposite of what is being built and anybody changing a plants page cannot tell what has already been ruled. Bringing the ledger and the register up to date by the set's own change procedure gives every later plants change one place to record its ruling.
acceptanceCriteria: A decision that changes a high-risk plants behaviour an earlier ledger entry settled is held in the set's decisions ledger as a new numbered entry whose status reads current, naming who decided it, the date it was decided and the entry it supersedes (repo:plantsfrontend src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/panel/README.md:25-35; src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/decisions.json)

Each ledger entry one of those decisions replaces stays in the ledger with its status reading superseded and names the entry that replaced it (repo:plantsfrontend src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/decisions.json:136-138)

Each subject one of those entries settles reads the resolution now in force: a conflict carries that resolution, who resolved it and the new entry's number, and a behaviour carries its status, the new entry's number and the resolution appended to its detail (repo:plantsfrontend src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/panel/README.md:25-35)

Each entry of the set's conflicts register whose disagreement one of those decisions settles points at that decision's ledger entry for the answer, and reads that entry's resolution and who made it (repo:plantsfrontend src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/conflicts.json; src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/panel/README.md:5-6)

The set's review-panel dockets and critic entries carry the arguments they already carry, and the ledger and its subjects are the only records a changed ruling rewrites (repo:plantsfrontend src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/panel/README.md:25-35)

sources.ref: the plants journey spec ruling deleted rather than superseded
every picker pages at eight and keeps the restatement of the chosen address, the plants contact picker included

rows.gate: Read the set's rulings records against the rulings they record: each new ledger entry with the entry it supersedes and the date it was decided, each replaced entry marked superseded, each re-stamped subject, and each register entry pointing at its ledger entry. Check that the later plants rows recorded their own rulings the same way.
rows.notes: Combines the ledger slice (req-2481) with the conflicts register slice (req-2483): the register holds no answer of its own, only a pointer at the ledger, so a register entry cannot be written without its ledger entry, and building the two apart would repeat the same reading of the set's change procedure for no gain. c-448 is settled by precedence: the plants journey spec ruling that was deleted rather than superseded is not restored, and nothing is added to record its removal. c-449 is settled by precedence too: every plants picker pages at eight and keeps the restatement of the chosen address, which the set's records already describe, so the pickers need no ledger entry and no record changes for them. The rulings whose plants behaviours earlier ledger entries settled are ruling:sam-2026-10-26 (save and return makes the same checks as save and continue on every plants page), ruling:sam-2026-11-19 (the notification task list heading shown visibly in plants, and one form per posting button on the plants notification view header) and ruling:ian-2026-11-25 (the pickers, which need no entry). Re-stamping a behaviour subject edits the set's journey specification, which the specification row also rewrites, so this row builds before it.

rows.title: The high-risk plants journey specification says what the set now has
rows.detail: The specification is the plants set's contract and the tests linked to its scenarios are its evidence, so an entry that reads the old way makes the contract false and points its evidence at behaviour nobody has. Several entries describe as unfinished work that is finished: every one of its sources is marked as still being extracted, it says the journey's end-to-end walkthrough fixture and the table of contract tests do not exist although both are in place, it still weighs keeping services the set has removed, and an empty fixture sits beside it seeding nothing. It also covers none of the amend, cancel amendment, delete notification and party edit pages the service serves, so their headings, fields and messages are specified nowhere. Putting each entry right makes the contract true.
acceptanceCriteria: Each of the specification's seven sources is recorded as extracted (repo:plantsfrontend src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/journey-spec.json:10, 17, 24, 31, 38, 45, 52)

The specification records the journey's end-to-end walkthrough fixture as in place, and names the consignment it opens with: ware potatoes from Spain notified before arrival (repo:plantsfrontend src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/journey-spec.json:240; src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear/flow/fixtures/happy-path.json:2-3)

The specification records the set's table of contract tests as in place, pinning that each collecting page's valid save commits exactly the answers that page collects (repo:plantsfrontend src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/journey-spec.json:222)

The specification's entry for the set's unused services records their removal as the settled outcome, for the import reason and purpose, the transport reference and the commercial transporter (repo:plantsfrontend src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/journey-spec.json:367)

The specification covers the amend, cancel amendment, delete notification and party edit pages the service serves, each with its heading, its fields and its messages (repo:plantsfrontend src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/journey-spec.json:711-1100)

The set keeps one end-to-end walkthrough fixture for the journey, held with the journey's flow, and the specification names it as where the walkthrough starts (repo:plantsfrontend src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/fixtures/happy-path.json:1)

Each of the specification's page, obligation and behaviour entries reads the same as the page, obligation or behaviour the service serves, checked entry by entry against the journey (repo:plantsfrontend src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/journey-spec.json:740-1100)
rows.notes: One slice: the specification is one document and its entries are read together, so splitting the finished-work corrections from the page, obligation and behaviour entries would mean reading the same file twice. Builds after the rulings-records row, which re-stamps behaviour subjects in this same specification. The picker entry already describes eight addresses a page with pagination beyond that and an inset naming the address chosen, which c-449 keeps, so criterion 7 leaves it as it reads. Criterion 7 is checked against the journey as the service serves it when the row builds; each later plants page change lands its own specification update in the same increment, which the combiner should carry as an invariant rather than a dependency on another theme's rows. The specification invents no Welsh wording for the pages and fields new to plants, which is its own standing rule and not drift.

rows.title: The high-risk plants set's guides describe the journey the service serves
rows.detail: The set's own record of documentation drift treats a document stating something the service does not do as a defect, because a second, false specification gets read as though it were current. The served-surface reference, the guide to the set's features, the guide to the journey's flow and the table of each page's copy state all describe the journey as it stood before this work. Bringing each one to what the service does, and writing into the set's documentation that a guide changes in the same increment as the behaviour it describes, puts the drift right and stops it returning.
acceptanceCriteria: The set's served-surface reference describes the notification dashboard and the address picker as the service serves them, the picker showing eight addresses a page (repo:plantsfrontend src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/docs/README.md:81, 83, 91)

The guide to the set's features describes how a page ends, and what a draft's and a submitted notification's view header carries, as the service has them (repo:plantsfrontend src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/docs/features.md:95, 178)

The guide to the journey's flow lists the journey's sections, its task rows in the order the overview lists them, where Back goes on every journey page, and which pages carry which caption, as the journey's flow has them (repo:plantsfrontend src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/docs/journey-flow-and-gates.md:21, 63, 111, 248)
The table of each page's copy state lists every page in the set with the state of its copy review (repo:plantsfrontend src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/docs/copy-status.md:3)

The set's documentation states that a guide describing a behaviour of the journey changes in the same increment as that behaviour (repo:plantsfrontend src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/backlog-extras.json increment docs-drift-sweep)
rows.notes: One slice: the four guides describe one journey and a reader checks them together, so correcting them apart would repeat the same walk of the journey four times. The set's testing guide is left alone: it is the test-hygiene branch's to change. The wording of the consignment contact page's two return controls, which the features guide records as that page's exception, changes with the page itself on the consignment-parties branch, in the same increment as the behaviour, so this row leaves that passage to it. The five untruths the set's own documentation-drift chore names are in code comments and in the recipes rather than in a guide stating a journey behaviour, so they stay the set's own chore and get no row here.

splitOff.why: It rewords the two return controls on the high-risk plants consignment contact page, whose copy, controller and tests are all in the consignment contact select feature folder that theme consignment-parties owns, together with that page's end-to-end test. The passage of the set's features guide that records the page as the one exception changes in the same increment as the wording, so it goes with it rather than with the guides row here.
